title: Ireland – Engineering works and construction works – Modification notice to CFT 3109037 Award of Contract for Waste Removal and Wall construction to Breffni Building and Civil Engineering Ltd
description: This Contract Award Notice is acting as a Modification Notice under Article 72 of 2014/24/EU to CFT 3109037 Contract for Darndale Park Waste Removal and Wall Construction to Breffni Building and Civil Engineering. Description of the procurement at the time of conclusion of the contract: The Contract comprises clearance and removal of approximately 40,000 tonnes of illegally dumped waste material and construction of boundary treatments and 117m of new 2.5m high precast boundary wall and footpath between Darndale Park and a group of Traveller Accommodation site known as the Northern Sites on the north side of Dublin within the boundaries of Darndale and Priorswood. The works shall include site clearance, removal of all waste material (investigations suggest non-hazardous), removal of asbestos, removal of end-of-life vehicles and other electrical goods, treatment and removal of invasive species, construction of concrete boundary walls, construction of new footpath, environmental monitoring. There is a requirement for removal of hazardous waste should it be encountered. Temporary works shall include construction of a construction stage haul road through Darndale Park to provide site access and all associated reinstatement works, protection to all existing services, fencing of works areas etc. Design of temporary works shall form part of the works. Changes arose in the following areas which were instructed in accordance with the provisions of the Public Works Contract - Removal and disposal of additional waste - Removal and disposal of horse carcass, contaminated waste, oil - Removal and disposal of large amount of historic concealed waste - Filling of excavated area with Article 27 backfill - Continued delays due to local obstruction of drainage construction - Construction of a new watermain that burst during excavation for drainage - Extensions of time under contract

title: Technical project support to BioClime
description: The project BioClime is working towards the implementation of the Paris Agreement and the Global Biodiversity Framework, the thematic focus of the requested services is closely tied to the Agreements and corresponding biodiversity and climate policies. A unique feature of the project is its emphasis on synergistic actions in the context of biodiversity and climate action. This entails a range of topics, including but not limited to ecosystem-based adaptation, nature-based solutions, biodiversity and climate mainstreaming, gender, water, forest and climate financing, deforestation-free supply chains, resource efficiency, circular economy, plastics, transformation of energy systems, and UN negotiations. Specifically, in the framework of technical support delivered to the project"s initiatives and its outputs, the contractor"s work will focus inter alia on the following core topics: - Biodiversity-Climate-(Water-)Nexus o Alignment between biodiversity and climate change policies and plans such as NDCs, NAPs, NBSAPs (e.g. assessments, goal and target setting, identification of strategies, financing and implementation, monitoring, reporting and stocktaking) o Synergies and cooperation among climate change, biodiversity and water relevant conventions and bodies at UN level o Synergies at science-policy level, (e.g. IPBES, IPCC) o Synergies at national and local implementation level (e.g. governance, spatial planning) with a focus on synergistic actions such as Nature-based Solutions (NbS) and ecosystem-based approaches, ecosystem integrity, ecosystem services. - Implementation of the requirements of the international climate negotiations of the UNFCCC o Agriculture, Forestry and other Land use (AFOLU) o Follow up Process on the Global Stocktake of 2023 under the Paris Agreement (GST) o Global Goal on Adaptation (GGA) o Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC), Long-term Strategies (LTS), Low Emission Development Strategies and Carbon Neutrality, National Adaptation Plans (NAP), adaptation communication o Climate Justice and equity o Legal aspects of UNFCCC/Paris Agreement; climate negotiations - Implementation of the requirements of the international biodiversity negotiations of the CBD o National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs) o Biodiversity and Climate Change o Biodiversity Monitoring, Reporting and Review; National Reports o Biodiversity Finance and incentive systems o Biodiversity Mainstreaming into sector policies, strategies and plans o Biodiversity inclusive Spatial Planning o Protected Area Management and other effective conservation measures o Ecosystem governance (e.g. via Indigenous peoples and local communities) o Legal aspects of CBD and UNFCCC; climate negotiations - Forests and Climate Change o International forest-related climate finance (e.g. mechanisms and instruments) and related policy processes, especially at international level (e.g. Forest Climate Leaders Partnership, GN2U, forest-related climate finance commitments under the UNFCCC) o Forest carbon markets (voluntary and compliance) o Deforestation-free supply chains and related legislation (e.g. EU Deforestation Regulation) as well as policy processes, especially at international level (e.g. Amsterdam Declaration Partnership and FACT Dialogue) - Further Climate and Biodiversity related Policies o Sectoral Policies and crosscutting topics: resource efficiency, circular economy, bioeconomy, plastics, sustainable production and consumption, transformation of energy systems as levers for transformational change o Land and soil management, forest landscape and ecosystem restoration o Integrated water resource management - Mainstreaming of biodiversity and climate policies, and coherence with other agendas o NDC and NBSAP governance and implementation o Vertical and horizontal mainstreaming of biodiversity protection, ecosystem services, climate mitigation and adaptation into development planning and public budgets o Climate Finance o Adaptation-Mitigation-Development-Nexus and Coherence - BMUKN supported initiatives: o NDC Partnership o NBSAP Accelerator Partnership o ENACT (Enhancing NbS for an Accelerated Climate Transformation) Partnership o PANORAMA Solutions - Gender, Diversity and Vulnerable Groups o Gender and the Biodiversity-Climate-Nexus o Gender and Climate Linkages o Gender and Biodiversity Linkages The general objective of the requested services is to support BioClime in the processing and implementation of specific tasks and consulting services for the BMUKN and partner countries Indonesia, Brazil, Mexico, and Thailand, within these thematic areas and to assume a service provider function. The contractor is responsible for providing the following work packages: Work package 1: Advisory and technical knowledge services (contributes to Output I, II, III, IV & V) Work package 2: Technical conceptualization and implementation of events, trainings and capacity development formats (contributes to Output III & IV) Work package 3: Editorial Services and Communications (contributes to Output I, II, III, IV & V)

title: NETWORKED ORBITAL MOBILITY FOR ROBOTIC ASSEMBLY/DEPLOYMENT (NOMAD) - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop orbital mobility system allowing robots to move themselves and tools/materials/components over very large networked space structuresDescriptionThe next stage of space utilisation may see finally extremely large space systems being deployed for the benefits of humanity. These systems (such as sunshields, Space Power Stations) will be of dimensions unseen before (km scale). The systems will rely on structures formed by truss elements interconnected in a rigid network.The construction of these structures will rely solely on robots. These robots will move along the structure while building, populating and maintaining it. At the same time, they will carry components and parts for the construction and/or maintenance. Considering the size of the network of truss elements, it is possible that tens of robots may have to travel over cumulated distances of hundreds of kilometres.While free-floating robotscould be envisaged for this task, safety concerns and the consideration that propulsion requires consumable make this option not attractive. An efficient and safe way to allow mobility over the network is to embed an electric mobility means within the structure.The subject of this activity is a networked mobility system that will be embedded in the truss elements of very large orbital structures, allowing robots to efficiently and quickly reach all accessible locations of the large structure for transporting components or tools. The system shall be built by the same robots that will use it, together with the truss element to which is attached. The system shall provide power to the robots travelling over it and allow multiple robots to travel over it without obstructing each other.This activity builds on the results of TDE activities (T713-601MM - Multi-arm Installation Robot for Readying ORUS and Reflectors MIRROR ; T713-701MM In-Space Assembly And Construction technologies ISAAC) to provide a comprehensive solution for extremely large structures.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Literature survey of applicable principles of mobility from terrestrial and space uses- Definition of conceptual design, system requirements- Preliminary design, identification of subsystems, interfacesand associated requirements- Breadboarding of critical capabilities and small scale testing- Development of critical components and testing against relevant space environmental factors- Development of large scale ground based demonstrator and validation

title: Siivouspalvelut - Arktinen avaruuskeskus
description: Hankinnan kohteena on siivouspalvelut Sodankylään, Ilmatieteen laitoksen Arktiselle avaruuskeskukselle. Hankinnan tavoitteena on tarkoituksenmukainen siivous, jotta pinnat ja materiaalit kestävät suunnitellun elinkaarensa ajan. Siivous suunnitellaan ja toteutetaan siten, että tiloissa tapahtuva toiminta on mahdollista. Tavoitteena on ylläpitää vaadittua puhtaustasoa. Tilat siivotaan vähintään palvelukuvauksen mukaisesti ja muut palvelut sovitun mukaisesti. Sopimuksen perusteella on mahdollisuus hankkia sekä varsinaisella sopimuskaudella että mahdollisina optiovuosina tarvittava määrä lisäsiivouspalveluita. Perussopimuskausi on kaksi (2 ) vuotta ja se alkaa sopimuksen allekirjoittamisesta. Sen lisäksi tilaajalla on mahdollisuus kahteen (2) yhden (1) vuoden mittaiseen optiokauteen. Tämän käyttöönotosta päätetään erikseen ja siitä ilmoitetaan kaksi kuukautta etukäteen. Arvioitu sopimuskausi 2+1+1 vuotta. Tarjouspyynnössä esitetyt hankintamäärät ovat arvioita, eikä sopimus muodosta tilaajalle määräostovelvoitetta tai palveluntuottajalle yksinoikeutta tuottaa palvelua.

title: INVESTIGATION OF FLIGHT WORTHINESS OF GROUND AND TACTICAL GRADE COOLERS AND ASSOCIATED DRIVE ELECTRONICS EXPRO+
description: Objectives of the Activity:The objectives of this activity are the following:1)To define at high level two strawman NewSpace-type missions/instruments that could require the use of ground coolers in space:a.One mission based on miniaturized Rotary Stirling Cooler (with or without IDDCA).b.One mission based on linear cooler (Pulse Tube or Stirling Cooler)2)To derive the two corresponding sets of technical requirements applicable to the Cryocooling Systems (including the electronics). 3)To propose, in collaboration with the cooler providers, a cost-effective documentation, PA/QA testing and verification approach that will ensure that theproduct will comply with the set of technical requirements identified before.4)To apply the recommended screening/testing sequences to at least one rotary and one linear ground based coolers coming from different suppliers.5)To collect the lessons learnt in terms of screening/testing and potential design adaptations while maintaining the price point of such cooler.The activity shall be performed in collaboration between a main contractor (otherwise called prime) which shall be knowledgeable in NewSpace type of instruments and two different Cooler Manufacturers: one for the Rotary types coolers, and one for the Linear Type of Coolers.

title: STRATEGIC ADVOCACY FACILITY
description: The Strategic Advocacy Facility is a strategic Action Readiness instrument within ESA's Earth Action framework that enables the translation of EO innovation, science and applications into sustained operational uptake and impact, particularly within the impact finance ecosystem of International Financial Institutions, climate and environmental funds, and developing-country stakeholders. The Facility combines programme-level impact measurement and evidence generation, strategic partnership engagement, institutional advisorysupport, country-level uptake assessment, strategic intelligence, advocacy and communication within a single integrated framework. Building on the legacy and assets of the Global Development Assistance (GDA) programme, it establishes a common Theory of Change, monitoring and evaluation system, stakeholder engagement architecture and learning framework for Earth Action, while creating feedbackloops between implementation, partnerships, communication, programme governance and future RD investments. Through interconnected task setup, the Facility acts as a cross-cutting enabler that strengthens EO adoption, supports partner alignment, captures and communicates evidence of impact, and ensures that Earth Action activities can be scaled, mainstreamed and translated into long-term societal, environmental and development outcomes.
